plan: Plan track T15 (Bot complete) and ADR-043 (Bot: devices, pairing, control and safety); the computer plugin and the job worker serve OpenVibe.Actor and the Codes job runner (tracks T14/T17)
release: v0.63.0: worker nodes run CI checks. The installer adds Codes v0.8.0, whose `kind: 'check'` jobs run one GitHub Actions workflow job with act in host mode (OpenVibe.Run's checks scheduler places them), and fetches the pinned act release once, checked against its sha256, for every check job. A desk host installed with allow_desk is reported as a desk host (#171).
runtime: go 1.24 (one static binary per platform); plugins in Python 3; an ESP32 Arduino library
deployment: none of its own: people install it on their machines and robots (curl -fsSL https://openvibe.link/install | sh, or a release binary); it connects out to OpenVibe.Bot (wss://openvibe.bot/device) and pairs through OpenVibe.Bot or OpenVibe.Network. On 2026-10-22 production held 1 platform node with 4 pairings and 5 node principals on Network, and 3 robots with 5 devices on Bot.
features: Git on this computer (G3): `openvibe-link clone <link>` clones into the root you chose in Link after you approve it there, reporting progress to git.openvibe.codes; `openvibe-link git connect <link>` publishes the repositories under that root, read-only, browsed through Link while the machine is online, and carries a repository page's "Clone to <this computer>" to the same approval there

LOOI headlights: Bot's explicit on/off custom action reaches the community driver as kind "headlight" (never actuator), with provenance, 300 ms lifetime/250 ms deadline, 200 ms original reserve on receipt, expires_at_mono_ns on the shared clock, a 2 requests/second budget shared with local controls, and stage=headlight_pending/headlight_refused ack data

machine access: `openvibe-link access request|list|approve|deny|revoke` asks another paired machine for scoped agent, send, screen, desk, computer or worker use; the target tray answers Allow/Deny, the owner may only narrow the scopes and time, and every relayed use is verified against Network's signed grant, live revocation and the target's own level; the opt-in "Let my agents talk" directory and `openvibe-link mcp` (eight agent and machine tools) let local agent CLIs message each other across machines
pairing with a code approved on openvibe.bot (or through Network), one outbound WebSocket, no open ports
safety: deadlines, owner limits clamped before any driver, heartbeats and a deadman, a persisted stop and the local kill switch (openvibe-link stop)

plugins as separate processes (JSON lines): dryrun, adeept_adr036, cozmo, relay and ros2 (rclpy or rosbridge); the community LOOI driver's contract; signed community profiles (openvibe-link profile verify)

the computer plugin for OpenVibe.Actor: terminal, files, screen, input and its own browser, at the level the owner sets on the machine (observe, ask, trusted, full); approvals in the tray (Linux, Windows), a notification or openvibe-link approve
the live screen: the machine's screen on openvibe.bot for its owner only, up to 30 minutes
the job worker (--worker): sandboxed function, code and linux jobs, and the OpenVibe.Codes job runner

the machine's roles from the network's hub (codes.worker, desks.host, ai.host, bot.robot): read at check-in, kept, and applied to what the machine was installed for; the local configuration always wins

OpenVibe Connect shares (CON-4): `openvibe-link share <port>` serves the share this computer was picked for, with no key; every saved share is in `openvibe-link status` (address, connected or why not, requests) and stops when the Link stops
one-command install on a Raspberry Pi or other Linux robot (I2C, SPI, camera tools, kit detection)
system service on systemd, launchd and Windows (or a Windows sign-in start)
ESP32 library (OpenVibeLink): pairing, control link, drive and actuator commands, telemetry, heartbeat, deadman and stop

`openvibe-link exchange serve --model <id>`: serve a local Ollama/llama.cpp/vLLM model through an OpenAI-compatible listener and register it on OpenVibe.Exchange's endpoint-seller API with the person's OPENVIBE_DEVELOPER_KEY, then remove the offer on Ctrl-C

Link for Android (v0, android/): the same Go pairing and connection bound with gomobile, a Kotlin + Jetpack Compose app (Pair, Approvals with a fingerprint for money, passwords, deletions and new recipients, Activity, This phone), Stay connected as an opt-in foreground service, and Send to OpenVibe on the share sheet; no phone automation
notYet: code signing and notarization for Windows and macOS (the release has SHA256SUMS only)
a tray on macOS (approvals there are a dialog with Deny as its default)
the computer plugin's browser on Windows
